exposure: maternal characteristics (race, age, educational level, economic class, partnership status, employment status, number of previous births, pregnancy desire, prenatal care adequacy, previous delivery service)
outcome: presumable diagnosis of inadequate alcohol use during pregnancy
cohort: The study included 23,894 postpartum women interviewed in hospitals across Brazil.
finding: The national prevalence of alcohol use during pregnancy was 14%, with 10% having a presumable diagnosis of inadequate alcohol use, particularly among women with worse social conditions and other risk factors like smoking and inadequate prenatal care.
